changes: Scribe p2: the name 'Ādinakavi' is not supported. The only name-like element is 'śrī….kavileṣi (!)', probably '…kavir alekhi' ('…kavi wrote'), with the first part of the name lost. 'ādinakaveneti' is too corrupt to read. as_written, name and evidence changed to match; confidence stays low.
Month normalised to Āṣāḍha (written 'āḍhasya (!)'); weekday normalised to Monday (candravāsara).
Purpose cleared: '…ārthaṃ likhitaṃ' is cut off before the purpose word (svārtha/parārtha?), so the purpose cannot be stated.
Notes extended: the closing verse is corrupt, and the LS conversion is uncertain.

date.as_written: la saṃ 357 āḍhasya (!) kṛṣṇapakṣe navamasyāṃ candravāsare

notes: The scribe's name is mostly lost in a lacuna: 'śrī….kavileṣi (!)' is probably '…kavir alekhi' ('…kavi wrote'). 'ādinakaveneti (!)' is unclear; it might hide an instrumental name such as '(…)dinakareṇa' or 'Dinakara' (wild guesses only). Because it is unreadable, no second person is posited from it. '|| ārthaṃ likhitaṃ pustakaṃ' is missing the start of a purpose compound (svārthaṃ/parārthaṃ?). 'āḍhasya' stands for 'āṣāḍhasya'. The closing verse 'asurama.ūni…vahniḥ' is badly corrupt; it may be a stock benediction or a chronogram verse, and no persons can be taken from it. ce_approx uses LS+1119 = 1476; with the other LS epochs that have been proposed (e.g. +1107/1108) the year would be about 1464–1465.
